name: dev-kit
description: Plan-driven autonomous dev loop: /write-plan decomposes designs into one-verify tasks (1-2 tests + their implementation, roughly 5-10min; PLAN.md) with TDD enforcement (tier=standard: new-test-required, side-effect-free verify commands), /execute-plan runs tier-routed builders (builder/sonnet with two-phase [red]/[green] TDD dispatch committed separately, red failure confirmed by an orchestrator-run verify; builder-light/haiku) -> orchestrator verify gate (verify re-run before every review; failures never reach the reviewer and are logged as FAIL(verify-gate); auto-run restricted to package/build-script commands with destructive patterns banned) -> reviewer(read-only incl. no Bash-mediated edits; verdict-only fixed output with a requirement traceability table demanding measured evidence -- next-task briefing authored by the orchestrator; inputs limited to task line + diff + gate result + project CLAUDE.md; risk:high tasks reviewed by opus upfront) per task, plus stage-reviewer integration review at stage boundaries (briefing-excerpt inputs only), a conditional plan-approval gate for large plans (8+ tasks / 3+ stages / 5+ new files / schema-external-API-dependency changes; thresholds overridable), contract-first parallel execution (multi-role plans get a mandatory Stage 0 contract stage producing boundary files, contract tests, and per-role test doubles -- mock servers/response fixtures/scratch DB schemas -- all derived from a single contract source; cross-role verify dependence is banned: a task's verify may depend only on Stage 0 contract artifacts, never on another role's implementation or runtime state, with real-wiring checks split into a final integration stage and [P]-tagged tasks required to name the contract-artifact path their verify depends on -- violations show up as a greppable blank in the verify text; contract changes are stop-the-world), size-routed execution modes recorded in a PLAN.md header (S sequential / A single-session parallel with parallel reviews and interleaved slot scheduling / B user-approved headless track parallelism via per-track worktrees, file-ownership manifests, and status files -- never with --dangerously-skip-permissions; tracks self-terminate as BLOCKED on any confirmation-requiring command and cannot push or merge), with PROGRESS.md + per-task git commit logging (incl. task start timestamps), a /metrics command computing measured retry rate, per-task duration, wall-clock union, and parallel efficiency from existing logs only (unparseable fields reported as n/a, never estimated), zero-touch project setup (write-plan provisions mode-A prerequisites -- worktree declaration and test-resource rule -- directly into project CLAUDE.md, edits limited to PLAN.md + project CLAUDE.md; mode re-judged on plan edits with auto S->A upgrades, deferred A->S downgrades, B always approval-gated) plus an idempotent /migrate command for existing projects (mode stamping, provisioning, verify normalization to allowlisted scripts without changing verification strength; side-effecting verifies and shared-DB test configs are reported -- never auto-fixed -- and held out of resumption until the user decides), RESUME checkpoint blocks (stage boundaries + PreCompact hook flush), and file-based pause (.dev-kit-pause). Prompt-cache preservation: no CLAUDE.md edits mid-loop, CLAUDE.md-mutating tasks pinned to stage end, same tier/risk tasks ordered adjacently. Parallel [P] groups run in per-task git worktrees (opt-in via project worktree: declaration, default off -> sequential) with a post-merge integration verify gate. Ships a PreToolUse hook that denies destructive Bash commands (DROP/TRUNCATE/rm -rf/git reset --hard/docker volume rm), the entire revert category (git checkout <path>/restore/clean/stash/rm/branch -D/reflog expire; branch switching and -b allowed), and out-of-scope Edit/Write via .dev-kit-scope (per-project exceptions via .dev-kit-allow-destructive), plus a harden skill for evidence-backed environment hardening (DB privileges, backups, dev/prod isolation). Includes brainstorming/grill/docs skills plus systematic debugging (root-cause-first, reproduce->isolate->trace->fix) and repo self-audit, with strict/flexible discipline tagging. Adds an upstream screen-spec stage for UI features: brainstorming locks the screen list (strict minimum-safety) with per-screen actions, result feedback, and empty/loading/error states, walks core scenarios (happy + one failure path each) before saving docs/screens.md, and delegates a lo-fi HTML mockup to builder-light when there are 3+ screens; write-plan reads screens.md as input and requires role=frontend verifies to name their target screen as docs/screens.md#screen (strict -- UI tasks without a screen spec stop as DECISIONS, screen-changing stages get a stage-end screens.md update task); the reviewer traces per-screen action/feedback/state rows against a screens excerpt included in the briefing (conditional fifth review input), with test or pre-existing playwright-screenshot evidence only (never generated by the reviewer, code-reading inadmissible), and stage-reviewer/docs treat screens.md as a drift-scan target. Metrics honesty fix: the first output row must list the actually-parsed input files with per-file block counts (strict -- never template text, missing files printed as absent), duration medians are split three ways (first-attempt-only / tier=light-only / over-300m outliers excluded, each with n), and the count of tasks missing a red line is reported separately from unconfirmed red. Screen-spec targeting is defined by deliverable, not by web-UI presence: brainstorming classifies every design as ui=interactive (full screen procedure), static (reports/dashboard snapshots/emails -- pages/sections with no-data/partial/generation-failed states, one reader-path walkthrough, three heuristics) or none (CLI/library/batch, with a stated reason), asking the user when ambiguous and never narrowing to none on its own (strict); write-plan records it as a `ui:` PLAN.md header line (strict -- interactive/static require docs/screens.md or stop as DECISIONS), migrate adds a missing `ui:` line only after asking the user (no default guessing), and stage-reviewer warns when ui=none but the stage diff adds .html/.pdf deliverables.
